def find_max(words):

    return sorted(words, key=lambda x: (-len(set(x)), x))[0]


# Unit test for function find_max
def test_find_max():
    # Word with the most unique characters wins
    assert find_max(["name", "of", "string"]) == "string"
    assert find_max(["name", "enam", "game"]) == "enam"
    assert find_max(["aaaaaaa", "bb", "cc"]) == "aaaaaaa"

    # Tie on unique character count -> lexicographically smallest wins
    assert find_max(["apple", "pear", "grape"]) == "apple"
    assert find_max(["bca", "cab", "abc"]) == "abc"
    assert find_max(["xy", "yx", "ab"]) == "ab"

    # Repeated characters don't add uniqueness
    assert find_max(["banana", "bandana"]) == "bandana"
    assert find_max(["aaa", "aab", "abb"]) == "aab"

    # Single-element list
    assert find_max(["hello"]) == "hello"
    assert find_max(["z"]) == "z"

    # Case sensitivity: 'A' and 'a' are distinct characters
    assert find_max(["aA", "aa"]) == "aA"

    # Longer word with more unique chars beats shorter ones
    assert find_max(["cat", "elephant", "dog"]) == "elephant"

    # All identical words
    assert find_max(["same", "same", "same"]) == "same"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_find_max()
    print("All tests passed!")
